sovereign_country.strategic_role: 连接拉美市场的欧洲商贸桥梁、本地化仓配与数字游民签证

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Carbon-Fiber Milling and Brushless Motor Integration of FPV Drones

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European legal system; unitary national legislative framework with regional autonomous communities)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC): Arts. 20-31 (denomination and registered office), 22-26 (formation and deed), 28-34 (inscription), 58, 62, 64-68 (share capital, minimum EUR 3,000, in-kind valuation), 209-215 (administrative organ appointment); complemented by Ley 18/2022, de 14 de septiembre (SL de formación sucesiva and digital incorporation) and Real Decreto 1065/2007 (NIF regime).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) for denomination; Registro Mercantil Provincial de Madrid for inscription; Notaría (Notary Public) at the registered office seat; Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for the tax identification number.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) with attached Estatutos Sociales, filed as a 'primera copia autorizada' for inscription in the Registro Mercantil through the official instancia de inscripción.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard S.L.: minimum capital EUR 3,000 (LSC Art. 22.1), fully subscribed and paid in cash at constitution (Art. 62) or in kind with independent expert valuation (Art. 67); cash must be deposited in a Spanish bank escrow account (cuenta de capital) in the company's name and released only after Mercantile Registry inscription. Alternative under Ley 18/2022: 'S.L. de formación sucesiva' may incorporate with capital from EUR 1, subject to a mandatory legal reserve of at least 20% of profits, distribution/remuneration caps and audit triggers until the EUR 3,000 threshold is reached.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [ALTAIR FPV DRONES S.L.] ADOPTED IN WRITING ON [DATE]: (1) The share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid up by the founding members into the escrow account, is hereby deemed validly constituted; (2) The registered office is fixed at [address], Madrid, Spain, within the jurisdiction of the Registro Mercantil de Madrid; (3) The following officers are appointed: [Name] as Sole Administrator (Administrador Único) exercising all legal powers, and [Name] as Non-Director Secretary; (4) The Administrator is authorized to obtain the provisional NIF, open corporate bank accounts, execute registration filings, and take every ancillary act required to perfect the incorporation. Registration before the Mercantile Registry and the deed publication are approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the Negative Denomination Certificate with the Central Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC), Madrid — counter service or 'Media Notaría' online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the official solicitud de certificación negativa de denominación listing at least three preferred corporate names (e.g., 'ALTAIR FPV DRONES, S.L.'). Pay the official tasa (approx. EUR 25) and obtain the certificate within 3-5 business days; the certificate is valid for 3 months and must be attached to the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Formulario de solicitud de certificación negativa signed by each founder
Photocopy of DNI/NIE/passport of each founding member
Payment receipt of the RMC official fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen name coincides with an existing registered company, the RMC rejects only that name; refile immediately with the next preferred alternative from the list. No substantive appeal is available against name collision, but the certificate may be renewed once if the deed is delayed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Capital Escrow Bank Account (Cuenta de Capital Provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution branch (e.g., Banco Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank, Banco Sabadell)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Founders open a provisional account in the future company's name, deposit the full EUR 3,000 minimum capital, and request a 'Certificado de depósito de capital' stating the account holder, deposit date and balance. The certificate is delivered to the notary for attachment to the deed and the funds remain blocked until registry inscription.
required_dossiers: Certificación negativa de denominación (in force)
Valid ID of all signatories (DNI/NIE/passport)
Bank account opening forms and AML/PEP declarations
Written declaration of source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML queries, provide a source-of-funds declaration and a memorandum of the FPV drone manufacturing purpose; if the account remains blocked, choose another accredited bank and reopen the escrow. Funds are non-withdrawable until presentation of the registry inscription certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario (Notary Public) at the seat of the registered office, Madrid (free choice of notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding members appear personally or by attorney before the notary, declare the S.L. form, approve the Estatutos (corporate object covering ISIC 3240/NAICS 339930 carbon-fiber milling and brushless motor integration of FPV racing drones), and deliver the denomination certificate and the bank deposit certificate. The notary verifies legality, reads the deed, and issues the Escritura Pública de Constitución with first authorized copies for registry and NIF purposes.
required_dossiers: Certificación negativa de denominación (valid)
Certificado bancario de depósito del capital social (EUR 3,000)
DNI/NIE/passport of every founding member
Draft Estatutos sociales (bylaws) including SL rules and corporate object
Independent expert valuation report if in-kind contributions (e.g., CNC milling equipment)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary questions the object (e.g., confusion with aviation operation law), file a rectification note clarifying that the company only manufactures and sells drone components and does not provide air navigation services; alternatively, select another notary in the same or an adjacent notarial district.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Delegación o Administración de Madrid; Documento 036 channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after execution, submit Modelo 036 (declaración censal) with the first authorized copy of the deed to request the provisional NIF (art. 43 del Real Decreto 1065/2007). The provisional NIF enables bank account activation and supplier invoicing and is automatically converted to the definitive NIF once the Mercantile Registry inscription certificate is filed.
required_dossiers: Primera copia autorizada de la Escritura de Constitución
Modelo 036 signed by the administrator with the activity code CNAE 3240
Power of attorney or authorization of the legal representative, if any
Proof of tax domicile (lease contract or ownership title)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT files a discrepancy, correct the census data via supplementary Modelo 036 and present the rectified deed page. The provisional NIF expires after 6 months and may be renewed; if expired, reapply with the updated deed and a certified copy of the pending registry application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Company in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial de Madrid (jurisdiction of the registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the 'primera copia autorizada' of the notarial deed together with the official instancia de inscripción and the self-liquidated registry tariff at the Provincial Registry. The registrar verifies the statutory legality of the deed, the capital deposit and the appointment of officers; upon approval, the inscription (hoja registral) is made and the company acquires legal personality.
required_dossiers: Primera copia autorizada de la Escritura Pública (first authorized copy)
Certificación negativa de denominación original
Instancia de inscripción (Registradores de España form)
Self-liquidated fee receipt of the Registro Mercantil tariff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar files a 'calificación' with defects, cure the observations by obtaining a complementary notarial resolution (acta complementaria or escritura de subsanación) and refile within the legal term; a total refusal may be appealed to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Completion: Definitive NIF, ITPAJD-AJD Liquidation and Municipal Activity Start-Up Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT; Consejería de Hacienda de la Comunidad de Madrid (ITPAJD); Ayuntamiento de Madrid — Sede Electrónica (license unit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, present the registry certificate to AEAT to convert the provisional NIF into definitive. Within 30 business days of the deed, self-liquidate Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados (Modelo 600) on the incorporation deed. Finally, update Modelo 036 with the definitive NIF, open the company's tax and labor registrations (IAE), and file the municipal comunicación previa/declaración responsable for the activity license (CNAE 3240) together with the technical file of the workshop.
required_dossiers: Certificación del Registro Mercantil acreditativa de la inscripción (hoja registral)
Escritura de constitución and Modelo 600 autoliquidación (ITPAJD-AJD)
Modelo 036 updated with the definitive NIF and IAE high
Municipal dossier: memoria de actividad, floor plans, lease/title deed, ITE certificate, noise and dust-control technical report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT or the municipal file is queried, submit the technical report of the carbon-fiber milling process (filtration, acoustic insulation) and the waste registration; for a municipal license delay beyond the legal term, invoke the positive administrative silence mechanism of Ley 39/2015 and, if required, obtain a judicial recognition order.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Economía, Hacienda y Empleo — Dirección General de Industria, Energía y Minas de la Comunidad de Madrid (industrial supervision) and Ayuntamiento de Madrid — Área de Gobierno de Economía, Innovación y Hacienda, Departamento de Licencias de Actividad (granting of the opening permit)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia municipal de actividad y apertura / Declaración responsable de comunicación ambiental (Clasificación CNAE 3240) under Ley 2/2012 (Comunidad de Madrid) and the municipal ordinance for classified activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) — Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental, with the regional Dirección General de Sostenibilidad y Cambio Climático de la Comunidad de Madrid
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Annex II, Group C (light manufacturing) under Ley 21/2013 — not subject to full EIA; the modular FPV drone workshop triggers a municipal 'comunicación ambiental / licencia de actividades clasificadas' and, only if installed milling capacity or raw-material input exceeds Annex II thresholds, a simplified 'evaluación ambiental de proyectos' (DIA shortened procedure)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to municipal sewer per Real Decreto 817/2015 limits (COD ≤ 500 mg/L, SS ≤ 300 mg/L, pH 6-9; no Annex III heavy metals), with no process discharge if dry milling is adopted; VOCs: no solvent consumption above 0.5 t/y so exempt from Real Decreto 117/2003 solvent plan — otherwise a solvent management plan is mandatory; dust: carbon-fiber milling requires absolute (HEPA) dust extraction and workplace OELs per INSST (inhalable nuisance dust ≤ 10 mg/m³, respirable ≤ 4 mg/m³); waste: non-hazardous carbon-fiber cutoffs and packaging registered as waste producer under Ley 7/2022 and Real Decreto 180/2015 (hazardous resins/cleaners manifested and removed within 6 months)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate per Real Decreto 513/2017 (RSCIEI) for a small industrial unit with low fire load; building structural capacity and stability certificate (ITE/Inspección Técnica de Edificaciones) covering machine vibration loads; occupational risk-prevention plan and work-station clearance (machinery guards per Real Decreto 1215/1997, chemical agents per Real Decreto 374/2001) jointly certified by an accredited Servicio de Prevención Ajeno (SPA) before commissioning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Sede Electrónica at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) must obtain a Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) for the company from AEAT. The procedure begins by submitting Form 036 (Censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores) before the start of business activity. For a foreign-owned SL, the incorporator or administrator may apply online with a certified electronic signature or through a tax representative. The NIF is issued immediately or within a short administrative window after verification of the deed, registration in the Registro Mercantil, and identification of the ultimate beneficial owner. The SL also needs a NIF for the non-resident shareholder if the shareholder is a legal entity, and the shareholder may need a NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) for natural persons. AEAT will assign a provisional NIF during incorporation and a definitive census NIF once the company is fully registered. In practice, the agent or administrator must request the definitive NIF within two months of the provisional NIF and provide the inscription certificate from the Commercial Registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not apply a check-the-box regime. A Spanish SL is per se a corporation subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades). Available elections include the option for consolidated taxation under the Régimen de Consolidación Fiscal where the parent holds a controlling interest, the patent box regime, R&D tax credit applications, and the election to be classified as a reduced-size entity (Empresa de Reducida Dimensión) for tax purposes. Hybrid mismatch rules derived from ATAD are implemented under Law 5/2022, and taxpayers must adjust for any hybrid mismatch outcome. No separate pass-through or check-the-box election exists for an SL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA) – Value Added Tax (VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general de minimis turnover threshold for domestic supplies. Any individual or entity performing a taxable business activity in Spanish territory is required to register for VAT by filing Form 036 as part of the census declaration. For intra-Community distance sales of goods, a €10,000 annual threshold applies across the EU; once exceeded, the seller must register in the Member State of the consumer or use the One-Stop Shop (OSS) scheme. Export volume does not create a separate VAT registration threshold – the exporter must be VAT-registered to issue invoices and claim zero-rating on exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: For general VAT compliance, Spain has not implemented a mandatory real-time clearance stamp for all invoices. However, the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) system is mandatory for large taxpayers (those with turnover exceeding €11.4 million), requiring near-real-time electronic transmission of invoice records to AEAT within 8 days (4 days for requested records). All B2B transactions with public authorities must be invoiced through the Facturae format and the general electronic invoicing point. Under the Crea y Crece Law, electronic invoicing is progressively being generalised for all business-to-business transactions, but the implementation is phased and not yet universally mandatory. There is no API-based stamping protocol equivalent to the Portuguese ATCUD or Italian SdI; the SII is the closest to a digital clearance mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating applies to goods physically leaving the territory of the European Union. The supplier must dispatch the FPV drones from Spain to a non-EU destination, transfer ownership to the non-resident customer, and retain documentary evidence of the actual departure from EU territory within the legally required timeframe. For services, zero-rating can apply to certain services directly linked to exported goods (e.g., transportation, handling, or ancillary services) and to certain offshore services supplied to an established non-EU customer, provided the recipient has a non-resident status and the service is effectively consumed outside the EU. The exporter must also ensure that the VAT ID and commercial documentation clearly identify the goods as exports. Export declarations must be made through the TARIC customs tariff and the electronic DUA system.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA – Documento Único Administrativo) submitted to the Customs and Excise Department of AEAT
Commercial invoice with explicit reference to the export goods and terms of sale (Incoterms)
Bill of Lading (for sea freight) or Airway Bill (AWB) or CMR transport document (for road freight)
Proof of actual departure from EU territory – boat manifests, landing certificates, or electronic TARIC departure notification
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment evidence showing the sales price has been paid or will be paid by the non-resident customer
Packing list and any additional customs certificates required for the specific machine type and lithium batteries, if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Export zero-rating is subject to strict documentary scrutiny by AEAT. If the exporter cannot produce the full export bundle at the time of an audit, AEAT may consider the zero-rating unfounded. The correction will be carried out by the tax authorities levying the unpaid VAT (21%), together with statutory late-payment interest (interés de demora). The inaccurate or incomplete documentation may also expose the taxpayer to a tax penalty graded from 50% to 150% of the amount improperly zero-rated, and in fraudulent cases the penalty can be escalated to the maximum bracket. Where the non-payment of the foreign customer is not attributed to export fraud but the zero-rating condition later fails, the exporter may be liable for the VAT amount and interest with possible penalty for negligence. In egregious cases, Article 201 of the General Tax Act can preclude the tax amnesty procedure and allow criminal fraud proceedings if the quantum exceeds €120,000 and wilful misconduct is proven.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain maintains full convertibility for both capital and current accounts under EU Treaty provisions and ECB oversight. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders face no regulatory hurdles beyond standard corporate tax filings and beneficial ownership documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or forced conversion applies to export receipts. Proceeds may be retained in foreign currency accounts provided they satisfy VAT obligations and corporate income tax requirements. No statutory conversion timeline or ratio exists.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility rating for PayPal and Stripe as target rails. Legal constraints are limited to PSD2 compliance and AML/KYC obligations for EU-domiciled SL entities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital KYC and director interviews are fully permitted for Spanish SL entities under current CNMV and Banco de España guidelines; physical appearance is not required unless enhanced due diligence is triggered.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for equity injections or capital contributions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish SL incorporation certificate, commercial registry extract, audited financial statements, and detailed business plan demonstrating legitimate carbon-fiber drone manufacturing revenue

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital transfers via SEPA credit transfers to Spanish IBAN accounts using purpose codes including 'CAPITAL_CONTRIBUTION', 'EQUITY_INJECTION', or 'SOCIAL_CAPITAL'. All transactions require full KYC, beneficial ownership verification, and supporting documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails comprise SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers and issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit for trade settlements. All disbursements must be supported by commercial invoices, packing lists, and VAT-compliant documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales): statutory balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, statement of changes in equity, and directors' report for the SL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil of the province of the registered office (Provincial Commercial Registry; coordination with the Registro de Titularidades Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary general meeting must approve accounts within six months of fiscal year end (31 December to 30 June); deposit with the Commercial Registry within one month of approval (deadline 31 July for calendar-year SLs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Full cierre registral (registry sheet blocked; no further corporate documents can be registered) until deposit is made (LSC Art. 282, Reglamento del Registro Mercantil Art. 378); administrative penalty of EUR 1,200 to 60,000 under LSC Art. 283, increased to a minimum of EUR 1,500 if delay exceeds six months; non-filing for two consecutive years triggers closure of the company's registry sheet and commencement of administrative strike-off or cancellation proceedings, with director joint liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax return (Modelo 200, Impuesto sobre Sociedades) reflecting the annual accounts and any required adjustment schedules for the SL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), national filing window through the Delegación Provincial of the SL's tax domicile
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year end; for a 31 December year end, no later than 25 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges of 5% (up to 3 months), 10% (3 to 6 months), 15% (6 to 12 months) or 20% (over 12 months) on the tax due plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75%); assessment penalties up to 50% of the omitted tax for deliberate understatement; criminal tax liability under Penal Code Art. 305 for amounts exceeding EUR 120,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation record for the SL's beneficial-ownership chain, submitted with and cross-referenced to the annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Titularidades Reales (RTR) of the Registro Mercantil (Ministry of Justice) and SEPBLAC AML supervisory network
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous disclosure duty: any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be filed within ten business days of the change; annual UBO re-confirmation runs concurrently with the annual accounts deposit (31 July for calendar-year SLs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative infringements under Law 10/2010 Arts. 42 to 46: penalties of EUR 10,000 to 60,000 for serious offences and EUR 60,000 to 600,000 for very serious persistent failures; registry sheet closure may be applied jointly by the Commercial Registrar.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (auditor de cuentas) if, for two consecutive fiscal years, at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded: total assets above EUR 4,000,000; annual net turnover above EUR 8,000,000; average workforce above 50 employees; below-threshold SLs may request a voluntary audit at the petition of shareholders owning at least 5% of share capital (LSC Arts. 264 and 265).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Real Decreto 1514/2007 Plan General de Contabilidad (Spanish GAAP, transposing EU Directive 34/2013/EU); IFRS-EU for groups with listed instruments and voluntarily for individual companies; the simplified PGC PyMEs framework applies to entities below EUR 5,700,000 turnover and related size criteria.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every SL share transfer is effective upon notarial execution and inscription of the acquirer in the Libro de Socios as of the transfer date; the company must report resulting beneficial-ownership changes to the Registro de Titularidades Reales within ten business days; the annual accounts deposit performs the annual UBO attestation, confirming the identity of all natural persons who ultimately own or control 25% or more of the share capital and exercise control through the board.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro de Socios (Register of Members with transfer annotations)
Libro de Actas (Minute Book of shareholders' and directors' meetings)
Libro Registro de Contratos con el Socio Único (Register of contracts with the sole shareholder, when applicable)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$ 220 to 950 per year for a registered-address plus administrative-agent package in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia or provincial capitals; local mid-market range US$ 300 to 600
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$ 2,500 to 8,500 for a statutory audit of a small-to-mid SL; US$ 1,200 to 3,000 for a voluntary limited review by an inscribed auditor (ICJCE) for entities below the mandatory audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate. Newly incorporated entities generally qualify for a 15% rate in the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory exclusions and eligibility conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying newly created entities and qualifying start-ups may apply a 15% rate under the applicable rules. Qualifying small enterprises may benefit from reduced rates under time-specific legislation. Research, technological innovation, investment, employment, audiovisual and other statutory tax credits may reduce the effective rate. The Spanish participation exemption may exempt qualifying dividends and capital gains, generally subject to a 5% deemed management expense and qualifying ownership, holding-period and anti-abuse requirements. Tax-loss utilization is subject to percentage limits based on prior-year net turnover, with a minimum taxable base generally preserved; additional limitations apply to large taxpayers and reorganizations.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite. Spanish corporate tax losses are not generally subject to a five-year expiry, but their annual utilization is subject to statutory percentage limitations and anti-abuse rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, annual Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency electronic headquarters (AEAT Sede Electrónica) using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve where permitted, or an authorized representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer closing on 31 December, the normal filing period is 1 July through 25 July of the following year. If the final day is not a business day, the electronic filing deadline follows the applicable administrative deadline rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the Spanish tax identification number (NIF), legal name, registered office, tax period dates, legal form, activity classification and filing type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or director does not replace the Spanish SL's NIF. Foreign persons and entities must use their Spanish NIF or NIE where required and provide foreign tax residence data only in the relevant related-party, withholding or annex fields.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report accounting profit or loss derived from statutory accounts prepared under the Spanish General Accounting Plan or applicable accounting framework.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income and expenses attributable to the Spanish taxpayer. Do not include the foreign owner's separate accounting results.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report permanent and temporary book-to-tax adjustments, including non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, limitation of financial expenses, related-party adjustments and other statutory items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish tax rules to the Spanish entity even where the underlying payment is booked to a foreign group. Cross-border payments must be reviewed for withholding tax, deductibility, beneficial ownership and transfer-pricing compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter utilized and available prior-period tax losses, subject to statutory utilization caps, minimum taxable income rules and anti-abuse provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign group losses cannot be imported into the Spanish SL unless a specific Spanish tax consolidation or legally recognized reorganization rule applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the adjusted taxable base, applicable corporate tax rate, tax liability before credits and any qualifying reduced-rate treatment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident owner does not by itself entitle the Spanish SL to a treaty rate. The Spanish SL generally applies the rate applicable to its legal form and qualifying tax regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim eligible credits and deductions supported by contemporaneous technical, accounting and documentary evidence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border research, financing or group-service arrangements require substantiation of Spanish activity, beneficial ownership, arm's-length pricing and economic connection to the Spanish business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit Modelo 202 corporate tax prepayments and other amounts already paid for the relevant tax period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments made by a foreign shareholder or group company are not automatically creditable against the Spanish SL's liability unless legally paid on its behalf and properly identified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile Spanish withholding tax credits, advance payments and the final balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividend, interest, royalty and service withholding generally requires separate Modelo 216 filings and Modelo 296 annual information reporting where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete relevant related-party, tax-haven, international transaction and group information fields, including information connected with Modelo 232 obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign related parties, intercompany loans, IP, services, guarantees, imports, exports and management charges consistently with the accounting records and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select payment, direct debit, refund or zero-liability outcome; attach or reference required schedules; submit electronically and retain the filing receipt and payment reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign representatives must hold valid authority and use an accepted electronic identification method. Payment from a non-Spanish bank must comply with AEAT payment-channel requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior AEAT demand generally gives rise to a surcharge of 1% plus an additional 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months. After 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus statutory late-payment interest. Filing after an AEAT demand or filing an incorrect return may trigger a penalty generally ranging from 50% to 150% of unpaid tax, subject to statutory aggravation and reduction rules. Late payment generates statutory late-payment interest and may lead to enforcement proceedings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, corporate income tax payment on account, filed electronically through AEAT Sede Electrónica. Modelo 222 applies where the taxpayer is part of a consolidated tax group.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment periods, generally in April, October and December
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 1-20 April, 1-20 October and 1-20 December. The calculation may be based on the prior-period tax liability or, where legally elected or required, the current-period accounting tax base. Calendar-day and banking rules apply to electronic payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter NIF, legal name, tax period and payment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's taxpayer identification and not the foreign shareholder's tax number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the applicable prior-year tax liability basis or current-period tax base, depending on the method used.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent-company accounting figures are excluded unless legally included through a Spanish consolidated tax regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the legally prescribed percentage and deduct eligible prior payments where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not apply treaty withholding rates to corporate income tax installments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the amount payable, payment method and bank or payment reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the payment account and electronic mandate are accepted by AEAT for cross-border payment arrangements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to make a payment on account can generate late-payment interest, collection surcharges and enforcement costs. Incorrect or omitted installment declarations may also produce tax penalties where the conduct causes an underpayment or obstructs tax administration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, informative return for related-party transactions and transactions involving jurisdictions classified as non-cooperative or tax-haven jurisdictions, filed electronically through AEAT Sede Electrónica where statutory thresholds are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the normal filing period is November.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report material related-party transactions by category, counterparty, amount, valuation method and applicable relationship.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include transactions with foreign parent companies, affiliates, directors, key management and entities under common control.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report transactions involving certain transfers of business, shares, real estate, intangible assets or other categories subject to specific reporting rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document valuation, ownership chain, legal agreements and commercial purpose for cross-border transfers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report transactions with persons or entities resident in jurisdictions covered by the applicable Spanish non-cooperative jurisdiction rules where thresholds or categories are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the current Spanish list and disclose payments, financing, IP and intermediary arrangements even if the immediate counterparty is not the ultimate beneficial owner.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file, late filing or materially incorrect filing may result in specific informative-return penalties under the General Tax Law, together with transfer-pricing adjustments, interest and additional penalties where unpaid tax results.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish non-resident income tax withholding generally applies to dividends paid by a Spanish company to a non-resident recipient. Domestic exemptions may apply, including the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive implementation for qualifying EU or EEA corporate parents generally holding at least 10% for the required uninterrupted one-year period, subject to anti-abuse, substance and beneficial-owner requirements. Treaty rates may reduce the rate, commonly to 5%, 10% or 15%, depending on the recipient, ownership percentage and applicable treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The recipient should provide a valid certificate of tax residence issued by its foreign tax authority before payment or otherwise maintain evidence supporting treaty entitlement. The Spanish payer must verify beneficial ownership, ownership and holding-period conditions, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose tests where applicable, and anti-abuse requirements. The payer generally applies the reduced rate at source when documentation is sufficient and files the relevant Spanish withholding return and annual information return. If excessive withholding was made, the non-resident may seek a refund through the AEAT procedure using the applicable forms and residence certificate. A treaty does not eliminate Spanish filing and record-keeping obligations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Spanish non-resident income tax rate is generally 24% for royalties, interest and other specified income paid to non-residents outside the EU/EEA, and generally 19% for qualifying EU/EEA recipients under current rules. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive may provide a 0% exemption for qualifying associated EU companies satisfying ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-owner and anti-abuse conditions. Tax treaties commonly reduce interest and royalty withholding to 0%, 5%, 8%, 10% or 15%, depending on the treaty. Technical services and other payments must be classified separately because domestic taxation and treaty treatment depend on the payment's legal and economic character.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spanish transfer-pricing documentation is generally not required for related-party transactions whose aggregate consideration with the same related party does not exceed EUR 250,000 during the tax period, calculated under the applicable statutory rules and subject to exclusions. A Local File is generally required when the documentation obligation is triggered. A Master File is generally required for a Spanish entity belonging to a group with prior-year consolidated net turnover of at least EUR 45 million, subject to statutory exemptions and content rules. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Modelo 232 has separate reporting thresholds, including the principal EUR 250,000 related-party transaction threshold and other category-specific tests.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no single standalone economic substance regulation equivalent to a separate ESR filing regime for ordinary Spanish SLs. Substance is nevertheless relevant under the General Tax Law anti-abuse rule, the principal-purpose and beneficial-ownership principles applicable to treaties and EU directives, controlled foreign company rules, participation exemption provisions, interest limitation rules and anti-hybrid rules. A Spanish company should maintain genuine functions, decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or business infrastructure proportionate to its activity, commercial risk, records, and control over assets and transactions. A conduit company, circular financing, artificial IP ownership, nominee management or unsupported management fees can result in denial of treaty or directive relief, income recharacterization, withholding assessments and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing sales, understating taxable income, creating false expenses, using fabricated invoices or transferring profits through non-arm's-length arrangements with the purpose of evading Spanish tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of unpaid tax, depending on the seriousness and aggravating circumstances, plus tax, interest and collection costs. Tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 per tax period may constitute a criminal offense, generally punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded. Aggravated cases may carry imprisonment of two to six years and a fine of two to six times the amount defrauded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face criminal liability, civil liability, tax subsidiary liability and disqualification where they participate in, authorize or negligently facilitate the conduct. Corporate limited liability does not protect individuals from personal criminal sanctions or statutory director-liability claims. Travel restrictions or precautionary asset measures are judicial and fact-dependent, not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting taxable sales, falsely claiming input VAT, issuing or accepting fictitious invoices, misclassifying goods, or using undeclared cash sales in drone, component or repair transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessments, late-payment interest and administrative penalties may apply, commonly calculated by reference to the unpaid or improperly credited tax. Serious or deliberate fraud may trigger criminal tax liability when the statutory tax-loss threshold is exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, accounting officers and persons who deliberately organize false invoicing may incur personal criminal and civil liability. Joint and several or subsidiary tax liability may arise where statutory management-failure conditions are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging unsupported royalties, management fees, financing costs, procurement margins or IP payments to foreign affiliates; allocating losses to Spain without functional justification; or failing to maintain reliable Local File, Master File or comparable evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may make an arm's-length adjustment, deny deductions, impose withholding tax, charge interest and impose transfer-pricing documentation or adjustment penalties. The absence or substantial defect of documentation can produce fixed penalties and, where a tax adjustment exists, percentage-based penalties under the General Tax Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability where they knowingly approve sham arrangements, conceal records or cause the company to incur tax liabilities through grossly negligent management. Ordinary technical errors do not automatically create personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal profit distribution and unlawful repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends without distributable profits, disguising dividends as loans or services, making shareholder withdrawals without documentation, or remitting interest, royalties or fees without applicable withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company may owe withholding tax, corporate tax adjustments, interest and penalties. Unlawful distributions may be recoverable under Spanish company law, and directors may be liable for resulting losses and creditor prejudice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be required to restore improperly distributed amounts, compensate the company or creditors, and face disqualification or insolvency-related liability. Criminal exposure may arise where the distribution is fraudulent or prejudices creditors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Spanish SL solely as a conduit with no genuine commercial activity, nominee directors, artificial offices, circular funds, pass-through dividends or IP ownership lacking personnel, control and risk-bearing capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Treaty or EU directive relief may be denied; income may be recharacterized; withholding tax, corporate tax, interest and anti-abuse penalties may be assessed. A shell company is not automatically unlawful, but artificial arrangements lacking economic substance are high-risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may incur tax, civil or criminal liability if they knowingly use the entity to conceal ownership, evade tax, launder funds or defraud creditors. Judicial asset measures and travel restrictions may be imposed in relevant proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained cash or crypto proceeds, concealing the ultimate beneficial owner, structuring payments, using nominees, failing customer due diligence, or processing funds inconsistent with the stated drone retail and manufacturing profile.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish AML breaches may attract administrative fines, including significant monetary penalties based on the applicable breach category and statutory maximums, together with public or professional sanctions. Money laundering can constitute a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment, fines and confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and controlling persons may be personally liable for knowing participation, willful blindness or serious compliance failures. Criminal conviction may result in imprisonment, disqualification, confiscation and judicial restrictions; travel bans are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying FPV drones, carbon-fiber components, batteries or motors; undervaluing imports; evading import VAT or customs duties; or importing restricted radio, battery or drone equipment without required conformity and safety documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs debt, import VAT, interest, seizure and administrative penalties may apply. Serious smuggling, forged documentation or prohibited-goods conduct may create criminal exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible import managers may be personally liable for deliberate customs fraud, forged records or prohibited imports. Corporate limited liability does not shield criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining false books, destroying invoices, backdating contracts, failing to preserve electronic payment records, obstructing AEAT inspection or repeatedly omitting mandatory returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax penalties, assessment by estimation, loss of deductions, enforcement costs and potential criminal liability may apply. Failure to comply with bookkeeping and inspection obligations can independently trigger statutory penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may be personally sanctioned or prosecuted for falsification, obstruction, concealment or deliberate destruction of evidence. Insolvency or creditor-prejudice consequences may also arise.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful employment and payroll tax practices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating employees as false independent contractors, paying undeclared wages, omitting social-security contributions, using undocumented workers or failing to withhold employment income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Employment, social-security and tax assessments, surcharges and administrative fines may apply. Severe exploitation, fraud or obstruction can create criminal liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers may be personally liable for unpaid withholdings, social-security amounts and deliberate labor violations. Criminal sanctions may apply in aggravated cases.
